description: Introduction and overview of the Scharnhorst-class Battleship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. Germany's Scharnhorst class — two ships — were fast 38,900-ton battlecruisers with nine 11-inch guns, built to raid convoys. Scharnhorst sank the carrier Glorious in 1940 but was herself sunk by Duke of York at the North Cape in 1943; Gneisenau was bombed out of the war. Baseline facts: German battlecruiser; 2 built; nine 11-inch guns; convoy raiders..
